description: We are GeoSAR Explorers, a team passionate about space technology, Earth observation, and understanding changes on our planet using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data. We are interested in satellite data analysis, remote sensing, AI/ML, and data visualization. We welcome enthusiastic team members with skills in Python, coding, Earth science, GIS, data processing, graphic design, and scientific communication who are eager to learn, collaborate, and innovate.
summary:
GeoSAR Explorers Exploring Earth's Changes Through Synthetic Aperture Radar.
GeoSAR Explorers is a project developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge "Dancing with the SARs." The project focuses on making SAR technology easier to understand and explore for monitoring changes on Earth's surface.
Natural disasters and environmental changes, including floods, deforestation, landslides and ground movement, can significantly affect communities and ecosystems. Traditional optical satellite imagery can be limited by clouds, smoke and darkness. SAR technology overcomes many of these limitations by using microwave signals to observe Earth's surface during both day and night and through most clouds.
Inspired by the NASA–ISRO NISAR mission, GeoSAR Explorers presents an organised workflow for exploring satellite observations, comparing radar images from different dates, interpreting possible environmental changes and communicating findings through understandable map-based visualisations.
The project highlights how radar observations can support flood monitoring, vegetation studies, land deformation research and environmental assessment. Its main objective is to connect advanced Earth-observation technology with accessible scientific information.
GeoSAR Explorers aims to encourage awareness, learning and informed environmental decision-making while demonstrating the potential of SAR technology to help us observe, understand and protect our changing planet.
details:
GeoSAR Explorers – Project Details

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

GeoSAR Explorers is an Earth-observation project designed to explain how Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) technology can help identify and understand changes occurring on Earth's surface. It is inspired by the NASA–ISRO NISAR mission and addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, "Dancing with the SARs."

The project follows four main stages:

Stage 1 – Explore: Identify a geographical area and explore available SAR observations or suitable sample datasets.

Stage 2 – Compare: Examine radar observations from different dates to understand differences in surface conditions.

Stage 3 – Interpret: Explore possible environmental changes, such as flooding, vegetation changes and land movement, while considering the limitations of radar interpretation.

Stage 4 – Communicate: Present the observations and their environmental significance through understandable explanations, maps and visual demonstrations.

2. What benefits does it provide?

SAR technology can observe Earth's surface during both day and night and through most cloud cover. This makes it particularly valuable when conventional optical satellite imagery is limited.

GeoSAR Explorers highlights the potential applications of SAR in flood monitoring, forest monitoring, wetland observation, coastal studies and land-deformation research. It also helps students and beginners understand how satellite radar technology contributes to environmental research.

3. What is the intended impact?

The main objective is to make advanced satellite observation technology easier to understand and explore. The project aims to encourage environmental awareness, improve understanding of disaster-monitoring technologies and demonstrate how Earth-observation information can support researchers, students, environmental organisations and communities.

In the future, the project could be expanded into a more advanced platform with verified satellite data integration, interactive map layers, automated change detection and downloadable environmental reports.

4. Tools, programming languages and technologies

The project draws on the following resources and technologies:

  • NASA–ISRO NISAR mission information and educational resources.
  • NASA Earthdata and official SAR learning materials.
  • Synthetic Aperture Radar concepts, including radar backscatter and multi-temporal observations.
  • Map-based visualisation and geographical information concepts.
  • Digital presentation and documentation tools.
  • ChatGPT as an AI-assisted tool for organising explanations and improving project documentation.

Python-based scientific data processing and GIS integration are possible future development directions. They should not be considered completed implementations unless they have been developed and tested. No dedicated hardware is required for the current demonstration concept.

5. What makes the project creative?

The creative aspect of GeoSAR Explorers is its effort to connect complex satellite radar technology with simple environmental explanations. Instead of presenting SAR only as a technical imaging system, the project organises the learning and exploration process into four understandable stages: Explore, Compare, Interpret and Communicate.

It connects the scientific potential of the NASA–ISRO NISAR mission with real-world environmental challenges and presents the information in a way that can be understood by people without an advanced remote-sensing background.

6. What factors did the team consider?

During project development and planning, the team considered:

  • Scientific accuracy when explaining SAR technology.
  • The importance of authentic NASA and ISRO mission information.
  • Availability and suitability of satellite observations.
  • Environmental relevance and potential real-world applications.
  • The limitations of radar backscatter interpretation.
  • Accessibility and simplicity of the project presentation.
  • The need for reliable validation before reporting environmental changes.
  • Future opportunities for technical development and expansion.

GeoSAR Explorers is an independent student project created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It is not an official NASA or ISRO product or an endorsed mission application.

Overall, GeoSAR Explorers aims to transform complex radar-observation concepts into accessible knowledge and inspire people to observe, understand and protect our changing planet.
